author: Anna Chen
title: Shenandoah County deputies seize over 100 farm animals in poor conditions; remains discovered on property - NewsBreak
text:
By Anna Chen Shenandoah County Sheriff's Office ,
1 days ago
Editor’s Note — The sheriff’s office released photos of the conditions the animals were found in. DC News Now has included those photos at the bottom of the story and is advising caution to readers, as they may be disturbing to some.
SHENANDOAH COUNTY, Va. ( DC News Now ) — Deputies conducted a search warrant in Mount Jackson last week after receiving reports that many farm animals were living in a decrepit manner.
The Shenandoah County Sheriff’s Office said its Animal Control Division received information that over 100 farm animals, including horses, cattle and donkeys, were living in “poor conditions.”
Court docs: Baby’s father arrested in 1998 Stratsburg cold case murder of missing infant’s mother Deputies conducted a search warrant, which took a span of three days, beginning on April 23 and ending on April 25. They found a large number of the farm animals on the property, many of which were “found in extremely poor condition and appeared malnourished,” the sheriff’s office said.
Some of the animals also showed visible signs of illness.
Deputies also found animal remains at multiple locations on the property.
“This large operation required 4 teams of VA veterinarians working to examine all of the animals on the property. The property was deemed inadequate living conditions for the animals, with an insufficient amount of food,” the sheriff’s office said.
A total of two donkeys, 84 horses and 66 cattle were seized.
(Shenandoah County Sheriff’s Office) (Shenandoah County Sheriff’s Office) (Shenandoah County Sheriff’s Office) There were over 60 law enforcement personnel and volunteers at the crime scene, processing it.
The investigation is ongoing.
